findings.how_to_check: Inspect MATCHING/results/fs_avg_performance_slides.tex and trace the Share validated rows back to val_fs30ml and valanc_fs30ml in MATCHING/fs_avg_performance.do:98, 105.
findings.suggested_fix: Relabel table rows as 'Middle-initial agreement among links (%)' and add a table note stating that this measures cross-census consistency, not ground-truth link accuracy.
findings.title: The slide table labels middle-initial agreement as validation without ground truth
findings.what_the_code_does: Computes cross-census middle initial equality via `mi1930==mi1940` (and `mianc1930==mianc1940`) conditional on both initials being non-empty and `linked_`c'==1`. In the output LaTeX table for slides (`fs_avg_performance_slides.tex`), these rows are labeled `Share validated (%)` and `Share validated, Ancestry initials (%)`.
findings.why_it_matters: Middle initials are noisy, non-unique, and subject to enumeration and transcription errors. Agreement across censuses is a consistency proxy, not ground truth validation; labeling it as validation in presentation slides violates the project standard that agreement is not accuracy.

findings.how_to_check: Compute agreement rates restricted to the intersection of records linked by all methods (linked_ans==1 & linked_true==1 & linked_fs30ml==1), and compare them to the method-specific averages currently reported.
findings.suggested_fix: Report validation rates on a common sample of links matched across all candidate methods, alongside a decomposition of added, dropped, and switched links.
findings.title: Validation rates condition on method-specific, endogenously selected link samples
findings.what_the_code_does: Generates `val_`c'' and `valanc_`c'' only when `linked_`c'==1`, and computes means using `summarize` over non-missing values. As a result, each column's validation share is evaluated on a different, method-selected subsample of individuals.
findings.why_it_matters: Changing transcription sources directly alters which records link. Hard-to-read names with lower literacy or atypical spelling link at different rates; differences in initial agreement across columns may reflect compositional selection of linked records rather than improved linkage quality.

findings.how_to_check: Count records in link1930_1940_fs1930_ml1940_cleaned_noraceblock0.dta where 1930 names match Ancestry vs. FamilySearch, and where 1940 names match Ancestry vs. ML.
findings.suggested_fix: Clarify in the column label or slide note that transcriptions are hybrid (e.g. 'FS 1930 (hybrid), ML 1940 (hybrid)'), and report the proportion of linked records utilizing non-Ancestry transcriptions in both years.
findings.title: Slide column header 'FS 1930, ML 1940' conceals field-by-field Ancestry fallbacks
findings.what_the_code_does: Labels the new column `FS 1930, ML 1940` without indicating that FamilySearch replaces Ancestry only when non-empty in 1930, and ML replaces Ancestry only when non-empty in 1940, while reporting `0.0` for `Links with an FS name in 1940 (%)` and omitting the ML utilization share.
findings.why_it_matters: The presentation table suggests a clean comparison between FamilySearch and ML models, but both sources retain substantial and potentially selective shares of Ancestry transcription baseline.

review_limits: No paper draft was supplied (per prompt instructions); claims-vs-code review was limited to claims, table headers, and notes generated in the code.
External data directories on F:\ and Dropbox were not available; sample sizes, match rates, and empirical estimates could not be computed at runtime.
The Stata pipeline and proprietary matching ado-files (abeclean, abematch) could not be executed; Stata behavior was inferred from source code inspection.
Untracked revision notes in review/revision-notes-2026-11-13.md contain editorial reminders that could not be verified against the manuscript.
structured_output.summary: The new mixed FamilySearch-1930 and ML-1940 matching pathway is mechanically wired with consistent parameter propagation, input validation, and separate slide output. However, the resulting slide table labels middle-initial agreement as 'validation' and evaluates each method on an endogenously selected, method-specific linked sample. The single most important fix is to relabel 'Share validated' as middle-initial agreement and caution that the comparison conflates linkage selectivity with transcription accuracy.

summary.description: Two to four sentences. The overall state of the reviewed work and the single most important thing to fix. No preamble.

dimensions_reviewed.description: Which scope dimensions were actually reviewed in this run.

findings.description: Defects and concerns, ordered most severe first. Empty if none. Do not pad with stylistic observations.

severity.description: blocker: a reported result is wrong. major: a referee would demand it. minor: real but survivable. nit: cosmetic.

confidence.description: verified: traced in the source. likely: strongly implied but depends on unseen data. speculative: a question, not an established defect.

title.description: One line, stating the defect itself, not its category.

location.description: path:line, or path:line-line. Several may be comma-separated. Required: a finding without a location is not a finding.

what_the_code_does.description: Precisely what the code computes, quoting the relevant expression. Contrast with what it was evidently intended to compute.

why_it_matters.description: The consequence for a number or claim in the paper. If there is no consequence, the severity is nit.

how_to_check.description: A concrete command, tabulation, or count the author can run to confirm or refute this in minutes.

suggested_fix.description: The change, specific enough to act on. Do not apply it yourself.

verified_clean.description: Things explicitly checked that were fine. This is what makes a short findings list trustworthy rather than lazy.

evidence.description: How it was confirmed, with path:line where applicable.

review_limits.description: What this review could NOT establish: data not readable, pipeline not runnable, paper text unavailable, Stata semantics not verifiable by reading. Be explicit; silence here reads as false assurance.
